candidates.exact_span: Regulations contained in 40 CFR §122.44 requires that NPDES permit limits are developed that meet the more stringent of either technology-based effluent limitation guidelines, numerical and/or narrative water quality standard-based effluent limits, or the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The more-stringent-of selection rule determines which numeric or narrative limit governs when technology-based, water-quality-based, and prior-permit limits could differ; a different reading of which limit set is controlling would change applicable discharge limits and exceedance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: Regulations found in 40 CFR 411.13 and 411.17 define BAT and BCT effluent limitations, respectively, for cement manufacturing non-leaching process, and 40 CFR 411.37 defines BCT effluent guidelines for materials storage piles runoff from cement manufacturing facilities.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which 40 CFR 411 subparts apply to cement manufacturing discharges frames which ELG-derived numeric limits are candidates for Outfall 001; interpreting the industrial category or subcategory differently could change which guideline-based limits are in scope.

candidates.exact_span: Effluent limitations established at Outfall 001 in the current permit regulate overflows from Quarry #1 pond which stores storm runoff and process water effluent from plant areas.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The scope of Outfall 001 (overflows from Quarry #1 pond; storm runoff plus process water) determines which discharge point, parameters, and flow types are subject to limits and monitoring; a narrower or broader reading of regulated overflows would change limit applicability and which monitoring obligations attach.

candidates.exact_span: The 40 CFR 411.37 ELG of 50 mg/l was the basis for establishment of TSS effluent limitation at Outfall 001.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage ties the operative TSS numeric limit at Outfall 001 to the 411.37 ELG value of 50 mg/l; interpreting whether that basis establishes a daily maximum, another averaging period, or a different enforceable form would change limit-applicability and exceedance calculations for reported TSS.

candidates.exact_span: EPA did not establish 40 CFR 411.13 temperature limitation at Outfall 001 because discharges at Outfall 001 would be intermittent and the permit restricted discharges due to catastrophic or chronic precipitation events.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether temperature limits apply, when discharges may occur, and when monitoring or compliance comparisons are triggered all hinge on interpreting intermittent discharge and precipitation-event restrictions; different readings would change which numeric limits apply, when monitoring is required, and how no-discharge or conditional periods are classified.

candidates.exact_span: The 40 CFR 411.17 TSS mass load limitation might not be applicable at Outfall 001 because the combination of storm runoff and process water.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The explicit uncertainty about 411.17 mass-load applicability means a different interpretation of how storm runoff and process water combine at Outfall 001 could include or exclude a mass-based TSS limit, changing which enforceable numeric limit is used for comparison.

candidates.exact_span: TSS reported maximum daily discharge did exceed the daily max limit of 50 mg/l.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This statement identifies a daily-maximum comparison metric and an observed exceedance of 50 mg/l; interpreting which reporting period or permit version it refers to, and whether daily max remains the operative compliance basis, would change exceedance determinations under Purpose A.

candidates.exact_span: As a result, it is proposed in the draft permit that the permittee report 30-day average for TSS.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A shift from daily-maximum to 30-day-average TSS reporting would change the applicable numeric comparison basis, impose a different monitoring/reporting obligation, and alter how missing or non-daily results are classified when ordinary numeric results are absent.

candidates.exact_span: Water quality-based requirements are necessary where effluent limits more stringent than technology-based limits are necessary to maintain or achieve federal or state water quality limits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether water-quality-based limits supersede the 411.37-derived 50 mg/l TSS technology-based limit depends on interpreting when WQBELs are necessary; a different reading could introduce additional or more stringent numeric limits for compliance comparison.
